featured.title: Heat sink for a 100 W CPU
featured.eyebrow: ENGG 114 Heat Transfer, Hofstra · Individual project · Spring 2026
featured.summary: Keep a 50.8 mm CPU at or below 85 °C while dissipating 100 W in 25 °C air on existing mounts. Sized a 15-fin Al 6061-T6 heat sink predicted at 69.85 °C (0.4485 °C/W) in MATLAB and 69.775 °C max in Fusion 360; cut mass 27.5% vs. 17-fin baseline (75.3 to 54.6 g). Bench test pending.

projects.title: Thermal model troubleshooting
projects.context: Stellant Systems co-op · ANSYS Mechanical · IronPython
projects.summary: Root-caused a non-physical 600 °C hot spot in an ANSYS Mechanical steady-state thermal model to a missing thermal interface material (TIM) layer; revised contact conductance from vendor data and re-meshed thin PCB/copper layers (body sizing, sweep, MultiZone), bringing predictions within 2–3 °C of test thermocouple readings. On a power-supply module, cut predicted junction temperature 57.6 °C (122.5 to 64.9 °C) with a gap pad, traded Al vs. Cu heat spreaders (recommending Al for mass and cost), and wrote an IronPython material-mapping script for a 327-body model. Described in words only; company drawings and data are proprietary.
projects.imageAlt: No public CAD image; proprietary co-op thermal model described in words only

projects.title: Heat sink for a 100 W CPU
projects.context: ENGG 114 Heat Transfer, Hofstra · Individual project
projects.summary: Designed a forced-convection 15-fin Al 6061-T6 heat sink for a 50.8 × 50.8 mm 100 W CPU (85 °C limit, 70 °C target, 25 °C ambient). MATLAB Nusselt resistance model predicted 69.85 °C (0.4485 °C/W), cross-checked against Fusion 360 steady-state FEA (69.775 °C max). Selected 15 fins over 17 to open fin spacing from 2.1125 mm to 2.557 mm and cut mass 27.5% (75.3 g to 54.6 g); authored a $376.92 Type-K thermocouple bench-test plan (experimental testing pending).
projects.imageAlt: CAD render of the 15-fin aluminum heat sink

projects.title: Lunar rover thermal control
projects.context: NASA L'SPACE Mission Concept Academy · Thermal Subsystem, Team 6 (training program)
projects.summary: Wrote the Mission Concept Review mission statement (scored 24/25, zero RFAs), Mission Operations ConOps, and 10 thermal control requirements (including a 480-hour lunar-night survival case), revised to be solution-neutral and verifiable after SRR-RFA-04. Owned 4 of 16 mission risks and flagged a heater energy shortfall (8,064 Wh worst case vs. 7,124 Wh battery; bounded across 4,987 / 6,072 / 8,064 / ~7,147 Wh cases). Planned MLI (~15 weeks) and heater (~9 weeks) lead times from public NASA contract data, co-built the $97K thermal budget, and drew the SRR thermal zoning schematic.
projects.imageAlt: No public schematic image; NASA L'SPACE Team 6 thermal requirements and energy-bounding case study

projects.title: Multi-diameter O-ring cutting fixture & silicone seal tooling
projects.context: Stellant Systems co-op · Autodesk Inventor · GD&T · FDM
projects.summary: Designed a multi-diameter O-ring cutting fixture in Autodesk Inventor across four FDM iterations with direct technician feedback, ASME Y14.5 GD&T, and tolerance stack-up analysis; documented the design in a first ECN (fixture now in shop-floor use). Also took a second mounting-plate fixture to manufacturing in 3 weeks, iterated a 3D-printed silicone syringe-pouring fixture through three versions, and designed a groove-matched silicone gasket and 3D-printed mold for an altitude-chamber vacuum leak test (leak test pending). Sanitized CAD models are viewable in the 3D Models Library.

projects.title: Vnua-Connect: student club operations platform
projects.context: Founder · 3rd Place ($150), Hofstra Lion's Den Pitch Competition (Nov. 2026)
projects.summary: Free, student-run app ('Giving clubs a chance') helping emerging Hofstra clubs move from interest group to university recognition (4 officers + 15 confirmed members tracker) and operate weekly without Excel, Google Forms, or GroupMe. Spring 2027 launch build adds an e-board hub ('My week', role-assigned recurring duties, Co-Presidents, role handoff binders, event volunteer slots with waitlist, short forms, agenda/minutes-to-tasks, Money ledger with CSV export, recognition roster CSV), non-AI behavioral features highlighted by Lion's Den judges (First-timer kit, greeter on duty, opt-in come-with-me buddy, arrival reminders, consented shout-outs, printable involvement record), Web Push queue with quiet hours, zero-build native ES modules, strict CSP, and Supabase Postgres RLS with SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
